title: Private communication from Pauli channels with no privacy
authors: Uthirakalyani G, Pritam Halder, David Elkouss
abstract: A channel capacity quantifies the communication capability of a noisy physical process. In contrast to communication channels in the classical world, quantum theory makes this capability contextual. We show that two Pauli two-qubit channels, each with zero private classical capacity, can be used to transmit private information when used together. One is a two-qubit Pauli channel whose environment can reconstruct the receiver output up to matrix transposition; the other is an antidegradable channel. We obtain a similar result when the second channel is the 50% qubit erasure channel. A simple binary code built from rank-three mixtures of Bell states activates private communication. The main ingredient in our construction is a transpose-antidegradable channel that is not antidegradable.
summary: This theoretical paper explores quantum channel capacity, specifically focusing on private information. The core finding is that two individual quantum channels, each incapable of transmitting private information, can be combined to create a joint channel that *can* transmit private information. This phenomenon, called superactivation, highlights the complex, non-additive nature of quantum communication capabilities.
main_problem: The paper investigates the phenomenon of 'private-capacity superactivation,' demonstrating that combining two quantum channels, each having zero private classical capacity, can enable the transmission of private information.
main_result: The authors show that two specific Pauli two-qubit channels, $F$ and $G$, can jointly transmit private information, achieving a positive private capacity even though $P(F)=P(G)=0$.
method: The analysis relies on defining private information using mutual information and analyzing the properties of quantum channels, specifically focusing on concepts like transpose-antidegradability and antidegradability.
model_or_system: The study uses abstract quantum communication channels, specifically Pauli two-qubit channels and the 50% qubit erasure channel, analyzed using Pauli operators and tensor products.
key_observables: Private classical capacity ($P(N)$), Mutual Information ($I$), and Coherent Information ($I_c$).
important_parameters: The zero private capacity condition is linked to the channel being transpose-antidegradable, while superactivation requires the joint channel to violate this property.
main_assumptions: The construction relies on the specific Pauli structure of the channels and the use of Bell states to build the activating binary code.
figures_summary: The notes reference tables detailing the action of Pauli operators on specific Pauli products and the resulting environment states after channel application.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining channel capacities and the zero-capacity condition (related to transpose-antidegradability) to constructing a pair of channels $(F, G)$ that exhibit superactivation, and finally extending this to include the 50% erasure channel $(F, H)$.
why_interesting: This work provides deep insights into the structural properties of quantum channels (degradability, antidegradability) and how these properties dictate fundamental communication limits, which is crucial for understanding quantum communication protocols.
